source.text: Καὶ ἤκουσα μεγάλης φωνῆς ἐκ τοῦ ναοῦ λεγούσης τοῖς ἑπτὰ ἀγγέλοις· Ὑπάγετε καὶ ἐκχέετε τὰς ἑπτὰ φιάλας τοῦ θυμοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ εἰς τὴν γῆν.

records.literal_gloss: And I heard a loud voice out of the temple saying to the seven angels: Go and pour out the seven bowls of the fury of the God into the earth.

en.L: And I heard a loud voice from the temple saying to the seven angels, "Go and pour out the seven bowls of the fury of God on the earth."
en.B: I heard a great voice speak from the temple to the seven angels: "Go and empty the seven bowls of God's fury onto the earth."
en.R: Then I heard a loud voice from the temple. It said to the seven angels, "Go and pour out the seven bowls of God's anger on the earth."

decisions.choice: a voice from the temple: God's own command
decisions.reason: No one could enter the temple until the plagues were done (15:8), so the voice from inside it is most likely God's.

decisions.choice: pouring out wrath: the prophets' language
decisions.reason: "Pour out your wrath on the nations" (Psalm 79:6; compare Jeremiah 10:25; Zephaniah 3:8). The bowls of chapter 15 are now poured.

source.text: Καὶ ἀπῆλθεν ὁ πρῶτος καὶ ἐξέχεεν τὴν φιάλην αὐτοῦ εἰς τὴν γῆν· καὶ ἐγένετο ἕλκος κακὸν καὶ πονηρὸν ἐπὶ τοὺς ἀνθρώπους τοὺς ἔχοντας τὸ χάραγμα τοῦ θηρίου καὶ τοὺς προσκυνοῦντας τῇ εἰκόνι αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And went away the first and poured out the bowl of him into the earth, and came a sore bad and evil on the men the [ones] having the mark of the beast and those worshiping the image of it.

en.L: And the first went and poured out his bowl on the earth, and a bad and evil sore came on the {{gender:people|men}} who had the mark of the beast and who worshiped its image.
en.B: The first angel went off and emptied his bowl on the earth, and foul, painful sores came on the {{gender:people|men}} who bore the mark of the beast and worshiped its image.
en.R: The first angel went and poured out his bowl on the land. Then terrible, painful sores broke out on the {{gender:people|men}} who had the mark of the beast and who worshiped its statue.

decisions.choice: an echo of the plagues of Egypt: sores
decisions.reason: Like the trumpets, the bowls recall the plagues on Egypt (Exodus 9:9-11; compare Deuteronomy 28:35). The bowls strike the whole of each realm, not a third: these are the last plagues (15:1).

decisions.choice: only on those with the beast's mark
decisions.reason: The sores strike those who took the mark and worshiped the image (13:16-17; 14:9-11). The mark they took in their flesh brings a wound in their flesh.

decisions.choice: poured out (L, R); emptied (B)
decisions.reason: The verb means to pour out; Balanced varies it with "emptied" to avoid repeating the same phrase seven times.

source.text: Καὶ ὁ δεύτερος ἐξέχεεν τὴν φιάλην αὐτοῦ εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν· καὶ ἐγένετο αἷμα ὡς νεκροῦ, καὶ πᾶσα ψυχὴ ζωῆς ἀπέθανεν τὰ ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ.

records.literal_gloss: And the second poured out the bowl of him into the sea, and it became blood as of a dead [one], and every soul of life died, the things in the sea.

en.L: And the second poured out his bowl into the sea, and it became blood like that of a dead [person], and every living soul died, the things in the sea.
en.B: When the second angel emptied his bowl into the sea, it became like the blood of a corpse, and everything that lived in the sea died.
en.R: The second angel poured out his bowl into the sea. The sea turned into blood like the blood of a dead body. Every living thing in the sea died.

decisions.choice: an echo of the plagues of Egypt: water to blood
decisions.reason: Like the trumpets, the bowls recall the plagues on Egypt (Exodus 7:20-21; compare Revelation 8:8-9, where a third of the sea died). The bowls strike the whole of each realm, not a third: these are the last plagues (15:1).

decisions.choice: poured out (L, R); emptied (B)
decisions.reason: The verb means to pour out; Balanced varies it with "emptied" to avoid repeating the same phrase seven times.

source.text: Καὶ ὁ τρίτος ἐξέχεεν τὴν φιάλην αὐτοῦ εἰς τοὺς ποταμοὺς καὶ τὰς πηγὰς τῶν ὑδάτων· καὶ ἐγένετο αἷμα.

records.literal_gloss: And the third poured out the bowl of him into the rivers and the springs of the waters, and they became blood.

en.L: And the third poured out his bowl into the rivers and the springs of waters, and they became blood.
en.B: The third angel emptied his bowl into the rivers and springs, and they turned to blood.
en.R: The third angel poured out his bowl on the rivers and springs. They turned into blood.

decisions.choice: an echo of the plagues of Egypt: the Nile turned to blood
decisions.reason: Like the trumpets, the bowls recall the plagues on Egypt (Exodus 7:19-24; compare 8:10-11). The bowls strike the whole of each realm, not a third: these are the last plagues (15:1).

decisions.choice: poured out (L, R); emptied (B)
decisions.reason: The verb means to pour out; Balanced varies it with "emptied" to avoid repeating the same phrase seven times.

source.text: καὶ ἤκουσα τοῦ ἀγγέλου τῶν ὑδάτων λέγοντος· Δίκαιος εἶ, ὁ ὢν καὶ ὁ ἦν, ὁ ὅσιος, ὅτι ταῦτα ἔκρινας, ὅτι αἷμα ἁγίων καὶ προφητῶν ἐξέχεαν, καὶ αἷμα αὐτοῖς δέδωκας πιεῖν· ἄξιοί εἰσιν.

records.literal_gloss: And I heard the angel of the waters saying: Righteous you are, the [one] being and the [one who] was, the holy [one], because these things you judged, \v 6 because blood of saints and prophets they poured out, and blood to them you have given to drink; worthy they are.

en.L: And I heard the angel of the waters saying, "Just are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, who is and who was, the Holy One, because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have judged these things, \v 6 because they poured out the blood of saints and prophets, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have given them blood to drink; they deserve it."
en.B: Then I heard the angel of the waters say: "Just are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, the one who is and who was, the Holy One, for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have judged in this way. \v 6 Because they poured out the blood of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} holy people and prophets, blood is what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have given them to drink. It is what they have earned."
en.R: Then I heard the angel who is in charge of the waters say, "You are fair in judging this way. You are the Holy One, who is and who always was. \v 6 These people killed {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} holy people and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} prophets. So {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have given them blood to drink. They deserve it!"

decisions.choice: the angel of the waters: the angel set over them
decisions.reason: Revelation speaks of angels with charge over parts of creation, the winds (7:1) and fire (14:18). Jewish writings of the time speak of angels over the waters (1 Enoch 66:2). This one declares God's judgment just, even in his own realm.

decisions.choice: who is and who was: no longer "who is coming"
decisions.reason: As in 11:17, the title lacks "who is coming": God has come in judgment. ὅσιος is the word of 15:4, "holy".

decisions.choice: blood for blood: a just recompense
decisions.reason: Those who poured out the blood of God's people are given blood to drink (compare Isaiah 49:26). The punishment matches the crime; the angel says it is deserved. This answers the martyrs' prayer of 6:10.

decisions.choice: saints (L); your holy people (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 5:8.

decisions.choice: you, your: deity pronoun setting
decisions.reason: The angel speaks to God.

source.text: καὶ ἤκουσα τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου λέγοντος· Ναί, κύριε, ὁ θεός, ὁ παντοκράτωρ, ἀληθιναὶ καὶ δίκαιαι αἱ κρίσεις σου.

records.literal_gloss: And I heard the altar saying: Yes, Lord the God the Almighty, true and righteous the judgments of you.

en.L: And I heard the altar saying, "Yes, Lord God the Almighty, true and just [are] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} judgments."
en.B: Then I heard the altar reply, "Yes, Lord God, the Almighty: {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} judgments are true and right."
en.R: Then I heard the altar say, "Yes, Lord God, the Almighty, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} judge in a way that is true and fair."

decisions.choice: the altar speaks: the voice of the prayers and the martyrs
decisions.reason: The souls of the martyrs cried out from under the altar (6:9-10), and the prayers of the saints rose from it (8:3-5). Now the altar agrees that God's judgments are just. The same words return in 19:2.

source.text: Καὶ ὁ τέταρτος ἐξέχεεν τὴν φιάλην αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τὸν ἥλιον· καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ καυματίσαι τοὺς ἀνθρώπους ἐν πυρί.

records.literal_gloss: And the fourth poured out the bowl of him on the sun, and it was given to it to scorch the men with fire.

en.L: And the fourth poured out his bowl on the sun, and it was allowed to scorch {{gender:people|men}} with fire.
en.B: When the fourth angel emptied his bowl on the sun, it was given power to burn {{gender:people|men}} with fire.
en.R: The fourth angel poured out his bowl on the sun. The sun was allowed to burn {{gender:people|men}} with its fire.

decisions.choice: the sun scorches: the reverse of 7:16
decisions.reason: Those who belong to God were promised that the sun would not strike them nor any scorching heat (7:16; Isaiah 49:10). Those who follow the beast are scorched.

decisions.choice: poured out (L, R); emptied (B)
decisions.reason: The verb means to pour out; Balanced varies it with "emptied" to avoid repeating the same phrase seven times.

source.text: καὶ ἐκαυματίσθησαν οἱ ἄνθρωποι καῦμα μέγα· καὶ ἐβλασφήμησαν τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ ἔχοντος τὴν ἐξουσίαν ἐπὶ τὰς πληγὰς ταύτας, καὶ οὐ μετενόησαν δοῦναι αὐτῷ δόξαν.

records.literal_gloss: And were scorched the men with heat great, and they blasphemed the name of the God the [one] having the authority over the plagues these, and not they repented to give to him glory.

en.L: And {{gender:people|men}} were scorched with great heat, and they blasphemed the name of God, who has authority over these plagues, and they did not repent to give {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} glory.
en.B: Burned by the fierce heat, {{gender:people|men}} blasphemed the name of the God who had power over these plagues; they would not repent and give {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} glory.
en.R: The terrible heat burned the {{gender:people|men}}. They said evil things against God, who had power over these plagues. But they would not change their ways and give {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} glory.

decisions.choice: blasphemy instead of repentance
decisions.reason: They know that God controls the plagues, yet they curse him instead of turning to him. After the witnesses rose, some gave glory to God (11:13), and the angel called all to give him glory (14:7). Here the hardening is complete, as with Pharaoh (Exodus 9:34-35).

source.text: Καὶ ὁ πέμπτος ἐξέχεεν τὴν φιάλην αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τὸν θρόνον τοῦ θηρίου· καὶ ἐγένετο ἡ βασιλεία αὐτοῦ ἐσκοτωμένη, καὶ ἐμασῶντο τὰς γλώσσας αὐτῶν ἐκ τοῦ πόνου, καὶ ἐβλασφήμησαν τὸν θεὸν τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἐκ τῶν πόνων αὐτῶν καὶ ἐκ τῶν ἑλκῶν αὐτῶν, καὶ οὐ μετενόησαν ἐκ τῶν ἔργων αὐτῶν.

records.literal_gloss: And the fifth poured out the bowl of him on the throne of the beast, and became the kingdom of it darkened, and they were gnawing the tongues of them from the pain, \v 11 and they blasphemed the God of the heaven from the pains of them and from the sores of them, and not they repented of the works of them.

en.L: And the fifth poured out his bowl on the throne of the beast, and its kingdom was darkened, and they gnawed their tongues because of the pain, \v 11 and they blasphemed the God of heaven because of their pains and their sores, and they did not repent of their works.
en.B: Then the fifth angel emptied his bowl over the beast's throne, and darkness fell on its kingdom. In their anguish people chewed their tongues, \v 11 and they blasphemed the God of heaven for their pains and their sores; yet they did not turn from their deeds.
en.R: The fifth angel poured out his bowl on the throne of the beast. Darkness covered its kingdom. People bit their tongues because of the pain. \v 11 They said evil things against the God of heaven because of their pain and their sores. But they would not stop doing evil.

decisions.choice: an echo of the plagues of Egypt: darkness
decisions.reason: Like the trumpets, the bowls recall the plagues on Egypt (Exodus 10:21-23). The bowls strike the whole of each realm, not a third: these are the last plagues (15:1).

decisions.choice: the throne of the beast: the center of its power
decisions.reason: The bowl strikes the seat of the beast's rule, the throne given it by the dragon (13:2). Its kingdom is plunged into darkness.

decisions.choice: their sores: the plagues pile up
decisions.reason: The sores of the first bowl still afflict them: the plagues do not pass but accumulate.

decisions.choice: poured out (L, R); emptied (B)
decisions.reason: The verb means to pour out; Balanced varies it with "emptied" to avoid repeating the same phrase seven times.

source.text: Καὶ ὁ ἕκτος ἐξέχεεν τὴν φιάλην αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τὸν ποταμὸν τὸν μέγαν τὸν Εὐφράτην· καὶ ἐξηράνθη τὸ ὕδωρ αὐτοῦ, ἵνα ἑτοιμασθῇ ἡ ὁδὸς τῶν βασιλέων τῶν ἀπὸ ἀνατολῆς ἡλίου.

records.literal_gloss: And the sixth poured out the bowl of him on the river the great the Euphrates, and was dried up the water of it, so that might be prepared the way of the kings the from rising of sun.

en.L: And the sixth poured out his bowl on the great river Euphrates, and its water was dried up, so that the way of the kings from the rising of the sun might be prepared.
en.B: When the sixth angel emptied his bowl on the great river, the Euphrates, its water was dried up so that a road would be ready for the kings from the sunrise.
en.R: The sixth angel poured out his bowl on the great Euphrates River. The water in the river dried up. This made a way for the kings from the east to come.

decisions.choice: drying up the Euphrates: a road for invading armies
decisions.reason: God dried up the Red Sea and the Jordan for his people (Exodus 14; Joshua 3), and Isaiah 11:15 speaks of drying up the River. The Greek historian Herodotus tells how Cyrus took Babylon by diverting the Euphrates and marching in along its bed. Here the drying opens a way for kings to come against God's people.

decisions.choice: the kings from the east
alternatives: the Parthian kings beyond the Euphrates
the kings of the whole world, gathered for the final battle
decisions.reason: In John's day the Parthians beyond the Euphrates were Rome's feared enemy (compare 9:14). In 16:14 the kings of the whole world are gathered for battle. The kings from the east may be part of that gathering, or stand for it.

decisions.choice: poured out (L, R); emptied (B)
decisions.reason: The verb means to pour out; Balanced varies it with "emptied" to avoid repeating the same phrase seven times.

source.text: καὶ εἶδον ἐκ τοῦ στόματος τοῦ δράκοντος καὶ ἐκ τοῦ στόματος τοῦ θηρίου καὶ ἐκ τοῦ στόματος τοῦ ψευδοπροφήτου πνεύματα τρία ἀκάθαρτα ὡς βάτραχοι·

records.literal_gloss: And I saw out of the mouth of the dragon and out of the mouth of the beast and out of the mouth of the false prophet spirits three unclean as frogs.

en.L: And I saw [coming] out of the mouth of the dragon and out of the mouth of the beast and out of the mouth of the false prophet three unclean spirits like frogs.
en.B: And out of the dragon's mouth, the beast's mouth, and the false prophet's mouth I saw three unclean spirits come, like frogs.
en.R: Then I saw three evil spirits that looked like frogs. They came out of the mouths of the dragon, the beast, and the false prophet.

decisions.choice: an echo of the plagues of Egypt: frogs
decisions.reason: Like the trumpets, the bowls recall the plagues on Egypt (Exodus 8:1-15). The bowls strike the whole of each realm, not a third: these are the last plagues (15:1).

decisions.choice: the false prophet: the second beast
decisions.reason: The beast from the earth (13:11-17), who deceives by signs, is now called the false prophet (19:20; 20:10). Dragon, beast and false prophet form a false trinity.

decisions.choice: spirits from their mouths: deceiving words
decisions.reason: The spirits come from their mouths: lies and propaganda that draw the nations to war (16:14). Frogs were unclean animals (Leviticus 11:10-12).

source.text: εἰσὶν γὰρ πνεύματα δαιμονίων ποιοῦντα σημεῖα, ἃ ἐκπορεύεται ἐπὶ τοὺς βασιλεῖς τῆς οἰκουμένης ὅλης, συναγαγεῖν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὸν πόλεμον τῆς ἡμέρας τῆς μεγάλης τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ παντοκράτορος Ἰδοὺ ἔρχομαι ὡς κλέπτης.

records.literal_gloss: For they are spirits of demons doing signs, which go out to the kings of the inhabited world whole, to gather them into the war of the day the great of the God the Almighty. \v 15 Behold I am coming as a thief.

en.L: For they are spirits of demons performing signs, which go out to the kings of the whole world, to gather them for the war of the great day of God the Almighty. \v 15 "Look, I am coming like a thief!
en.B: These are spirits of demons, doing signs, and they go out to the kings of all the world to assemble them for war on the great day of God, the Almighty. \v 15 "Look, I come like a thief!
en.R: They are spirits of demons that do miracles, called signs. They go out to the kings of the whole world. They gather the kings together for the battle on the great day of God, the Almighty. \v 15 "Listen! I will come when people do not expect me, like a thief.

decisions.choice: Christ's words break into the vision
decisions.reason: The words "Look, I am coming like a thief" and the blessing that follows (16:15) are spoken by Christ himself, breaking into John's account as a warning to the readers. The SBLGNT sets them apart from the narrative. In the source data the sentence divisions fall so that 16:15 is split across this record and the next; the record follows those divisions.

decisions.choice: the war of the great day of God
decisions.reason: This is the final battle, described in 19:11-21 and 20:7-10. "The great day" recalls "the great day of their wrath" (6:17) and the prophets' day of the LORD.

decisions.choice: coming like a thief
decisions.reason: See the note on 3:3.

decisions.choice: signs; miracles, called signs (R)
decisions.reason: As in 13:13.

source.text: μακάριος ὁ γρηγορῶν καὶ τηρῶν τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ, ἵνα μὴ γυμνὸς περιπατῇ καὶ βλέπωσιν τὴν ἀσχημοσύνην αὐτοῦ καὶ συνήγαγεν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὸν τόπον τὸν καλούμενον Ἑβραϊστὶ Ἁρμαγεδών.

records.literal_gloss: Blessed the [one] watching and keeping the garments of him, so that not naked he walks and they see the shame of him. \v 16 And he gathered them into the place the [one] being called in Hebrew Armageddon.

en.L: Blessed [is] the one who stays awake and keeps {{gender:their|his}} garments, so that {{gender:they may|he may}} not walk naked and people see {{gender:their|his}} shame." \v 16 And [the spirits] gathered them to the place that is called in Hebrew Armageddon.
en.B: How blessed is anyone who keeps watch and holds on to {{gender:their|his}} clothes, and so will not walk about naked with {{gender:their|his}} shame on view!" \v 16 And the spirits brought the kings together at the place called in Hebrew Armageddon.
en.R: God blesses the person who stays awake and keeps {{gender:their|his}} clothes on. Then {{gender:they|he}} will not have to walk around naked and be ashamed." \v 16 Then the spirits gathered the kings together at the place called Armageddon in the Hebrew language.

decisions.choice: the third blessing: staying awake and clothed
decisions.reason: This is the third of the book's seven blessings (1:3). Staying awake and keeping one's clothes means remaining faithful and ready (3:2-4, 18). To be found naked is to be put to shame at his coming.

decisions.choice: Armageddon: the mountain of Megiddo
alternatives: a real place where the final battle will be fought
a symbol of the final gathering of the nations against God
decisions.reason: The name is most likely Hebrew "Har Megiddo", "mountain of Megiddo". Megiddo overlooked a plain where famous battles were fought (Judges 5:19; 2 Kings 23:29; compare Zechariah 12:11), but there is no mountain of that name. The name may be a symbol for the place where the nations gather against God and are defeated.

decisions.choice: he gathered: the spirits are the subject
decisions.reason: συνήγαγεν is singular, but its subject is most likely the spirits of 16:13-14; a neuter plural subject in Greek can take a singular verb.

decisions.choice: the spirits; the kings (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the subject and the object (m3).

source.text: Καὶ ὁ ἕβδομος ἐξέχεεν τὴν φιάλην αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τὸν ἀέρα καὶ ἐξῆλθεν φωνὴ μεγάλη ἐκ τοῦ ναοῦ ἀπὸ τοῦ θρόνου λέγουσα· Γέγονεν καὶ ἐγένοντο ἀστραπαὶ καὶ φωναὶ καὶ βρονταί, καὶ σεισμὸς ἐγένετο μέγας, οἷος οὐκ ἐγένετο ἀφ’ οὗ ἄνθρωποι ἐγένοντο ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς τηλικοῦτος σεισμὸς οὕτω μέγας, καὶ ἐγένετο ἡ πόλις ἡ μεγάλη εἰς τρία μέρη, καὶ αἱ πόλεις τῶν ἐθνῶν ἔπεσαν· καὶ Βαβυλὼν ἡ μεγάλη ἐμνήσθη ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ δοῦναι αὐτῇ τὸ ποτήριον τοῦ οἴνου τοῦ θυμοῦ τῆς ὀργῆς αὐτοῦ·

records.literal_gloss: And the seventh poured out the bowl of him on the air, and came out a voice great out of the temple from the throne saying: It has happened. \v 18 And there were lightnings and voices and thunders, and earthquake happened great, such as not happened since men came to be on the earth, so great earthquake so mighty, \v 19 and became the city the great into three parts, and the cities of the nations fell; and Babylon the great was remembered before the God to give her the cup of the wine of the fury of the wrath of him;

en.L: And the seventh poured out his bowl on the air, and a loud voice came out of the temple, from the throne, saying, "It is done!" \v 18 And there were lightnings and voices and thunders, and there was a great earthquake, such as had not happened since {{gender:people|men}} came to be on the earth, so great an earthquake, so mighty, \v 19 and the great city split into three parts, and the cities of the nations fell, and Babylon the great was remembered before God, to give her the cup of the wine of the fury of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} wrath.
en.B: When the seventh angel emptied his bowl into the air, a great voice came out of the temple, from the throne: "It is done!" \v 18 Lightning, loud sounds, and thunder followed, and an earthquake struck so violent that nothing like it had ever happened since human beings first lived on the earth. \v 19 The great city was torn into three parts, and the cities of the nations fell. Babylon the great was not forgotten before God: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made her drink the cup of the wine of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} raging anger.
en.R: The seventh angel poured out his bowl into the air. A loud voice came from the throne in the temple. It said, "It is finished!" \v 18 There was lightning, loud noise, and thunder. And there was a terrible earthquake, the worst since people have lived on the earth. \v 19 The great city split into three parts. The cities of the nations fell down. And God remembered Babylon the great city. He made her drink from the cup filled with the wine of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} terrible anger.

decisions.choice: It is done: the last plague completes God's wrath
decisions.reason: Γέγονεν is perfect: it has happened and stands done. The voice from the throne declares the end of the series (15:1). The same word sounds again in 21:6, at the making of all things new.

decisions.choice: an earthquake like none before: Daniel 12:1
decisions.reason: Daniel speaks of "a time of trouble such as never has been since there was a nation" (Daniel 12:1; compare Mark 13:19). The signs of God's presence (4:5; 8:5; 11:19) reach their height.

decisions.choice: the great city: Babylon
decisions.reason: The great city is named in the same sentence: Babylon the great (compare 14:8; 17:18; 18:10). Its fall is told in chapters 17-18.

decisions.choice: remembered before God: God does not forget her sins
decisions.reason: To be remembered before God is to have one's deeds brought into judgment (18:5). The cup is the cup of 14:10; "the fury of his wrath" doubles the word for anger, as in 19:15.

decisions.choice: poured out (L, R); emptied (B)
decisions.reason: The verb means to pour out; Balanced varies it with "emptied" to avoid repeating the same phrase seven times.

source.text: καὶ πᾶσα νῆσος ἔφυγεν, καὶ ὄρη οὐχ εὑρέθησαν.

records.literal_gloss: And every island fled, and mountains not were found.

en.L: And every island fled, and mountains were not found.
en.B: Every island ran away, and the mountains were found no more.
en.R: Every island disappeared, and the mountains could not be found.

decisions.choice: islands and mountains gone: the world's foundations shaken
decisions.reason: In 6:14 they were moved from their places; here they vanish (compare 20:11, where earth and sky flee from God's presence).

source.text: καὶ χάλαζα μεγάλη ὡς ταλαντιαία καταβαίνει ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἐπὶ τοὺς ἀνθρώπους· καὶ ἐβλασφήμησαν οἱ ἄνθρωποι τὸν θεὸν ἐκ τῆς πληγῆς τῆς χαλάζης, ὅτι μεγάλη ἐστὶν ἡ πληγὴ αὐτῆς σφόδρα.

records.literal_gloss: And hail great as talent-weight comes down out of the heaven on the men, and blasphemed the men the God because of the plague of the hail, because great is the plague of it exceedingly.

en.L: And great hail, about a talent in weight, comes down from heaven on {{gender:people|men}}, and {{gender:people|men}} blasphemed God because of the plague of the hail, for its plague is exceedingly great.
en.B: Hailstones weighing about {{units:seventy-five pounds|a talent}} each came down out of the sky on {{gender:people|men}}, and they blasphemed God over the plague of hail, because the plague of it was very severe.
en.R: Huge hailstones fell from the sky on {{gender:people|men}}. Each one weighed about {{units:seventy-five pounds|a talent}}. People said evil things against God because the hail was so terrible.

decisions.choice: an echo of the plagues of Egypt: hail
decisions.reason: Like the trumpets, the bowls recall the plagues on Egypt (Exodus 9:22-26; compare Joshua 10:11). The bowls strike the whole of each realm, not a third: these are the last plagues (15:1).

decisions.choice: a talent: a very heavy weight
decisions.reason: A talent was the largest unit of weight, varying by region from about 55 to 100 pounds (25 to 45 kilograms). Hailstones of that size would crush whatever they struck.

decisions.choice: still no repentance
decisions.reason: As after the fourth and fifth bowls (16:9, 11), people blaspheme God instead of repenting.

decisions.choice: units: seventy-five pounds | a talent
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek measure; Balanced and Readable give a modern equivalent, with the original as the alternative (m2).
